name: Unsloth AI
subcategory: LLM fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning library, local training UI
origin_detail: Founded 2023 by Daniel Han (formerly at NVIDIA, where he sped up algorithms such as t-SNE; maintainer of Hyperlearn; known for reporting and fixing 20+ bugs in open LLMs such as Gemma, Llama, Mistral and Phi) and Michael Han; GitHub repo created 2023-11-29; Y Combinator Summer 2024; San Francisco.
flagship_projects: Unsloth Studio (local training and inference UI, AGPL-3.0, 2026)
Unsloth-optimised model uploads (GGUF and quantised weights)
openness_notes: Initial 2: the core library was Apache-2.0 from the first commit (2023-11-29), but by March 2024 the README advertised a closed 'Unsloth Pro' ('Open source trains 5x faster - see Unsloth Pro for up to 30x faster training!'), whose benchmark previews had 'code stripped out', linked to a pricing page. That is open core. Current 2 (low confidence): the core is still Apache-2.0, and the Studio UI added in March 2026 is AGPL-3.0 (OSI-approved copyleft); the 2026 README no longer mentions Pro, but the pricing page returned 403, so whether a proprietary tier still exists is unconfirmed. It would be 3 if there is none.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 open source plus proprietary Unsloth Pro / Max
license_history.note: README at commit 74f7968 (2024-03-27) benchmarks 'Unsloth Open Source' against paid Unsloth Pro and Max, linking to unsloth.ai/pricing

license_history.license: Dual: Apache-2.0 core + AGPL-3.0 optional components (Unsloth Studio UI)
license_history.note: LICENSE files changed with 'Studio (#4237)' on 2026-03-12; README: 'The core Unsloth package remains licensed under Apache 2.0' while 'certain optional components, such as the Unsloth Studio UI are licensed under the open-source license AGPL-3.0'

risk_events: Very small team (12 per the YC profile) maintaining a project with ~80K GitHub stars
Monetisation not visible in 2026: the Pro tier advertised in 2024 is absent from the current README and the pricing page could not be fetched
New 2026 code (Studio UI) released under AGPL-3.0 copyleft, which deters proprietary reuse; core stays Apache-2.0
robustness: Apache-2.0 core with ~7.5K forks could outlive the company; NVIDIA promotes it (NVIDIA blog tutorials, Oct and Dec 2025). Control is single-company with no foundation.
physical_science_relevance: Cuts the hardware needed to fine-tune open models on domain data (claims about 30x faster training with 90% less memory), so a lab with one GPU can adapt LLMs to scientific text or tasks.
openness_effect_assessment: Open-sourcing a fast fine-tuning library built a large following for a tiny team (~80K stars; YC profile claims over 10 million monthly model downloads). The closed Pro version advertised in 2024 has faded from view, and new code in 2026 was released under AGPL rather than a source-available licence. No revenue or funding figures were found, so the commercial effect of openness cannot be assessed.
key_takeaway: Unsloth is the small-team, kernel-optimisation case: a YC S24 startup whose Apache-2.0 library became a default way to fine-tune open models, with NVIDIA's backing in tutorials. It started as open core with a closed Pro tier, and in 2026 chose OSI copyleft (AGPL-3.0) for its new desktop UI rather than a non-OSI licence.
